subject: Confirm maintenance fall-through window & SLA remediation
messages:
From: Nathan Brooks <nathan@acme-payments.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: asha.verma@clearpay.io
Date: 2027-09-01T09:21:00Z
Subject: Observed 503 spike during your scheduled maintenance window

Hi Priya,

We saw a cluster of 503 responses between 09:03 and 09:16 UTC during what looked like Redwood's scheduled maintenance (per our calendar notice). Our checkout service experienced a ~12% failure rate for tokenization calls; I attached a small extract of our edge logs (acme-logs-0901.txt). Can you confirm whether this was maintenance-related and whether it qualifies for an SLA exception/credit?

We need a narrow window (start/end) and a causal tag for our ops and legal teams. Happy to hop on a quick call if useful — availability from 11:00–13:00 UTC today.

Thanks,
Nathan Brooks
SRE Lead, Acme Payments
attachments: acme-logs-0901.txt (text)
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan@acme-payments.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed 503 spike during your scheduled maintenance window

Nathan — thanks for the heads up and the log extract. We're investigating now. Initial notes: we did run a planned kernel upgrade in us-west-2 starting 09:00 UTC with an orchestrated rolling maintenance policy. It should have been transparent, but the telemetry team flagged some fallback evictions that line up with your window.

Can you confirm the exact request IDs/timestamps for the highest error bursts? Diego, Marcus — looping you in to pull the full trace bundle and a remediation recommendation.

I'll push a formal window confirmation and whether this meets SLA credit criteria by EOD; if we determine a service-level impact, we will propose a proportional credit and provide the postmortem timeline.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, nathan@acme-payments.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T12:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed 503 spike during your scheduled maintenance window

On Fri, Sep 1, 2027 at 09:21 Nathan Brooks <nathan@acme-payments.com> wrote:
> We saw a cluster of 503 responses between 09:03 and 09:16 UTC...

Hi all — attaching the internal trace bundle (redwood-trace-20270901.zip) and a short chronology. Summary:
- Maintenance start: 2027-09-01T09:00:00Z (rolling kernel upgrade across that shard pool)
- First anomalous error spike: 2027-09-01T09:03:12Z
- Peak 503 frequency: 2027-09-01T09:08:30Z to 2027-09-01T09:12:45Z
- Observable fallback: several nodes evicted due to a scheduling race; requests landed on a thin pool causing transient queue saturation and 503s.

Preliminary assessment: this was an operational maintenance that had an unexpected fallback path; it is not a customer-initiated configuration change. We should treat as a Redwood service-impacting event for SLA purposes unless legal or procurement indicate otherwise.

Action items:
- Marcus: quantify per-minute error rate vs baseline and compute proportional credit impact.
- Priya: coordinate with Acme on the exact request IDs for correlation.
- Diego infra: file RCA and postmortem draft within 5 business days.

Diego Fernandez
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-trace-20270901.zip (archive)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, nathan@acme-payments.com
Date: 2027-09-02T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed 503 spike during your scheduled maintenance window

Nathan, Priya — I ran the proportionality calc against Acme's committed SLO (99.9 availability for inference endpoint). Using our telemetry and the correlation window Diego provided, the effective downtime-equivalent is ~00:00:05.4 cumulative for the customer (weighted by traffic). Proposed credit: one-quarter of a monthly token bill for September per the SLA's pro-rata table.

Notes for legal: this was caused by our maintenance fallback; it was not caused by customer traffic or config. If Acme wants to dispute the proportional method we can walk through the math.

I'll include the short derivation in the postmortem.

Marcus Lin
SRE Metrics Lead, Redwood Inference
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan@acme-payments.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-03T14:05:00Z
Subject: Final: maintenance window confirmation, proposed remedy, next steps

Hi Nathan — thanks for your patience. To summarize and next steps: 

1) Confirmed window: 2027-09-01T09:03:12Z to 2027-09-01T09:12:45Z (observed elevated 503 rate that correlated to our maintenance fallback).
2) Root cause: rolling kernel upgrade triggered an eviction race that temporarily reduced capacity on a small subset of nodes (see Diego's bundle).
3) Proposed remedy: Marcus proposes a proportional credit equal to 25% of Acme's monthly token bill for September. We will submit the formal credit note via billing and apply it to the next invoice.
4) Postmortem timeline: draft RCA within 5 business days, final postmortem within 10 business days.

If that plan looks acceptable to Acme, I will open the billing ticket and schedule a short postmortem review with your ops and our infra team (30 min). If you want to contest the credit number, please flag specific points and we'll revisit the math.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
